title: A threefold cord (Ecclesiastes 4:9–12)
hookLine: two are better than one, and "a threefold cord is not quickly broken"
carry: woe to him that is alone

cards: Pull a single thread from the hem of a shirt and snap it between your fingers. Easy. Now take three threads, twist them together, and try again.
It bites into your skin. It holds. The strength isn't in one heroic strand.
It's in ordinary strands wound around each other. Kohelet, the man who called everything breath, noticed the same thing about people.

teach.b: Just before this passage, Kohelet describes a man entirely alone. No child, no brother, and yet no end to his work, and his eyes never satisfied with riches. He never stops to ask who he's laboring for.
That is hevel, Kohelet says. Breath.
Then he turns, in the King James words: "Two are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour." Three small pictures follow.
The first: "For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth; for he hath not another to help him up." A stumble on a road, and a hand reaching down.

The second: if two lie together, they have heat, but how can one be warm alone? The third: if one is attacked, two can stand against the attacker. Then the line that stays: "a threefold cord is not quickly broken."
Wait. He's been talking about two. Where does the third strand come from?
Some say it simply means: if two are strong, three are stronger still. Some see the third strand as God, woven between two people. Others see a community, the circle that holds a pair together.

teach.h: A THREEFOLD CORD IS NOT QUICKLY BROKEN.
teach.b: And notice the word quickly. Not never broken. A cord can still fray.
But wound together, it takes longer, and that gives time for someone to come and help.

how: Ecclesiastes 4:9–12 is studied in Jewish teaching on friendship and community, and some readers take the third strand as God between two people.

games.q: you're reading Kohelet. he's talked about two people, then says 'a threefold cord'. what is the third strand?
games.why: the text leaves it unnamed. some readers see God, some a community, some simply 'more is stronger'.

practice: Bring to mind someone you care about but haven't really talked to in a while, and picture where they might be right now and what their day looks like.

Think of one small thread you could add, a message, a question about something they care about, a memory you share. If you pray, you can pray for that friend by name; if not, hold their name gently for a while.
